units.unit: The student is working on an essay about rent control and the SDU market.
The student requests sources on the 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance and the SDU market generally, starting broad.
The source should back up a claim.
The student argues the 2021 ordinance is too weak.
The ordinance caps increases inside a tenancy but leaves the initial rent free.
Landlords jack up the first offer, which is the whole complaint.
The student wants core data plus elasticity and tenant survey.
The elasticity numbers are the spine of the essay.
The student wants material on what tenants actually say they want, such as surveys or a named tenant to quote.
The tenant material is the counterweight because the student's numbers all come from supply.
The student needs the demand side: what tenants themselves say, surveys, a named tenant, anything with a voice.
The student asks to bring back the doc with an NGO survey from the last list.
The student wants tenant-side voices and the NGO survey.
The student notes the first shortlist was mostly tenant stuff.
The student wants the other camp: landlord side or academic modeling.
The student wants the landlord association one and the elasticity paper.
The student wants to see what the landlord side claims about margins and whether the modeling backs the contraction story.
The student wants landlord claims and elasticity modeling, the other camp.
